function.name: areDeclarationFlagsIdentical
function.description: This function compares two TypeScript declaration objects to determine if they have identical declaration flags, taking into account specific allowances for differences in optionality between parameters and variable declarations. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

left.description: The first TypeScript declaration object to compare. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

right.description: The second TypeScript declaration object to compare. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

message.content:
Sure! To compare two TypeScript declaration objects—say `parameterObject` (representing a function/method parameter) and `variableDeclarationObject` (representing a class property or local variable)—you can use the `areDeclarationFlagsIdentical` function. Here’s how you’d invoke it:

```json
{
  "left": "{\"declarationKind\":\"Parameter\",\"flags\":{\"optional\":true,\"private\":false,\"protected\":false,\"public\":true,\"async\":false,\"abstract\":false,\"readonly\":false,\"static\":false}}",
  "right": "{\"declarationKind\":\"VariableDeclaration\",\"flags\":{\"optional\":false,\"private\":false,\"protected\":false,\"public\":true,\"async\":false,\"abstract\":false,\"readonly\":true,\"static\":false}}"
}
```

Replace the JSON strings above with the actual stringified versions of your `parameterObject` and `variableDeclarationObject`. The function will return an object indicating whether the flags match under the rules you described (e.g., allowing optionality differences but requiring all other flags to align).
